quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: The Strait of Juan de Fuca, which you can see from Port Angeles, was named after a Greek navigator who sailed for Spain in 1592. He claimed to have found a passage between the Pacific and Atlantic oceans, though this mythical waterway didn't exist—but his name lives on in your beautiful local waters!

short_read.title: Why Do Hummingbirds Hum?
short_read.teaser: These tiny jewels of the bird world don't actually hum with their voices—the sound comes from something surprising! Discover the delightful physics behind one of nature's most enchanting sounds.

medium_read.title: The Secret Language of Flowers in Victorian Times
medium_read.teaser: In the 1800s, people sent elaborate messages through carefully chosen bouquets—each bloom had a specific meaning. Learn how a simple nosegay could convey love, friendship, or even a gentle warning in this charming tradition.

long_read.title: Hungary's Thermal Baths: A Living Tradition
long_read.teaser: From Roman times to today, Hungary's thermal springs have been gathering places for healing, conversation, and community. This beautiful exploration takes you through the history and culture of Budapest's magnificent bathhouses.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season Ending
port_angeles.description: Late August marks the end of harbor seal pupping season in the Strait of Juan de Fuca. The adorable pups born this summer are now learning to fish on their own, and you might spot them playing near the shore at Ediz Hook or along the waterfront.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's wings can beat ___ times per second during normal flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! Those tiny wings are incredibly fast—almost too quick for our eyes to see!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 50 beats per second—amazingly fast for such a tiny bird!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those little wings beat about 50 times per second—that's what creates their distinctive humming sound!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: During courtship dives, male hummingbirds can beat their wings up to 200 times per second! This incredible speed requires a heart rate of over 1,200 beats per minute.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Ildiko! Pillangó is such a beautiful, lyrical word for these delicate creatures!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word is 'pillangó'—such a lovely sound for such a lovely insect! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is full of charming compound words and diminutives. The word 'pillangó' may come from 'pille' (flake or scale) referring to the delicate scales on butterfly wings.

puzzle_3.question: What percentage of the Olympic Peninsula is protected as national park or forest?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! About 90% is protected—you live in one of the most pristine wilderness areas in America! Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest preserve nearly the entire peninsula.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Actually, about 90% of the Olympic Peninsula is protected! You're surrounded by one of America's greatest wilderness treasures—Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest cover almost the entire area.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: This remarkable conservation means the Olympic Peninsula has some of the last intact temperate rainforests in the world, along with wild coastlines and mountain meadows that look much as they did centuries ago.
